correctness.rationale: Decaying tree shifts are norm limits of finite sums of strictly singular edge maps, while restriction to the root block proves that every nonzero word polynomial has a uniformly separated unit-vector image and is therefore noncompact.

originality.rationale: Qualified to the best of our knowledge. Searches found finite-direct-sum nilpotency results and general free-semigroup shift theory but no countable-tree construction embedding a free algebra into the strictly-singular/compact quotient. Classical sources not exhaustively inspected remain a residual risk.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a qualitative finite-versus-countable boundary: a quotient known to be nilpotent on the closest finite sums can contain a free noncommutative algebra on a concrete countable direct sum.
